summary: stellarfix ships and auto-executes a bundled Windows RAT on install
details: The package has no library or CLI surface: package.json ships only bin/ezfn.exe and postinstall.js, has an empty description, no author/homepage/repository, and restricts os to win32. The postinstall lifecycle hook (scripts.postinstall: 'node postinstall.js') unconditionally runs execFileSync on bin/ezfn.exe with inherited stdio, so `npm install stellarfix` on Windows executes the bundled binary with no user interaction. The bundled binary is a.NET assembly whose metadata is consistent with an njRAT/AsyncRAT-family remote access trojan: ClientSocket/BeginConnect/ConnectServer/ActivatePong C2 loop, SendBot and ChatID messaging, Antivirus/Exclusion routines for defender bypass, Spread for self-propagation, LoggerPath keylogging, avicap32.dll webcam capture, and RegistryKey CurrentUser Run-key persistence. Installing this package on Windows results in full-host code execution and persistent remote control by the operator of the embedded RAT.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
